reason: Records took the launched checkpoint's name as the identity of the model answering on the port, while an older server actually answered.
Incomplete running-chain checks, a missing lock and a stale lock are concurrency defects against the scripts' evident intent of one chain per experiment.
Reports and manifests were taken as recording the checkpoint's training inputs but reflected the working tree at scoring or resume time.
Falling strict-format probe scores were read as a loss of general capability even though correct values were scored as mismatches.
The scorer ignored the probe's own exact-comparison policy by matching the first number in the answer.
The option leaked the target's reference solution into demonstration selection, which the code was meant to exclude.
A validation slice dominated by trained plans and a repeatedly consulted holdout were treated as held-out evidence.
Appending unfamiliar wording was taken to isolate the effect of supplying correct inputs but shifted the prompt distribution.
The split function did not honour the declared evaluation reservations.
The retry loop recorded attempts without executing them, contrary to its purpose.
Base models' compiled-format scores were taken as their capability although they were never trained to produce that format.
An argument-parser bug made every launch exit, with the orchestrator's process-disappearance completion check a secondary record-state issue.
Scripts in the temporary directory were removed by a machine reset.
The disk filled and corrupted a checkpoint mid-save, a resource failure that the undersized guard failed to prevent.
A 'series done' log line written on failure too was taken as evidence of chain completion.
The driver's free-memory figure was taken as the system's available memory though reclaimable cache made it unreliable.
Scores with 45.7% missing responses on 705 items were compared with another model's score on a different 585-item set.
The experiment name 'qwen3-17b' was taken as the identity of a 17B model despite manifests saying 1.7B.
Exact string-match scores were taken as correctness although references held underivable wording.
Unrecorded subagent judgments were reported as measured semantic accuracy.
A causal explanation contradicted by the training records was asserted and acted upon.
A regression diagnosis asserted item-level facts before any failing item was read.
Scores on regenerated holdouts with changed items and oracles were compared as if on the same test.
An accuracy difference between models of different families was causally attributed to parameter count alone.
A result was attributed to container commands the saved programs did not use and over-generalized from one plan to a book.
A gain was credited to new commands that item-level evidence shows did not produce it.
The pruning procedure deleted run manifests that the stated retention intent required to be kept.
Files were deleted from the working directory by an unexplained outside cause and restored from version control.
A wrong number copied from a neighbouring row was written into a report table.
A reported plan count was miscounted by including held-out circuits' plans.
A range seen on winner checkpoints was over-generalized to all checkpoints.
The blind-solver procedure leaked stored reference solutions into an input meant to exclude them.
